items.text: AMEND AND RECOMMIT TO CONSUMER PROTECTION

items.actClause:
AN ACT to amend the general business law, in relation to the prohibition of
the sale of crib bumper pads and the restriction of the use of such pads in
certain settings
items.memo:
BILL NUMBER: S3788

SPONSOR: CARLUCCI
 
TITLE OF BILL:  An act to amend the general business law, in relation
to the prohibition of the sale of crib bumper pads and the restriction
of the use of such pads in certain settings

 
PURPOSE OR GENERAL IDEA OF BILL:

To ban the sale of crib bumpers pads and restrict their use in certain
settings. This bill will prevent the deaths of and serious injury to
infants which have been attributed to the use of crib bumper pads.

 
SUMMARY OF SPECIFIC PROVISIONS:

Section 1, subdivision 1, paragraphs (a) through (i) provides a defi-
nitions section, including a definition of crib bumper pads. The defi-
nition of crib bumper pads does not include vertical railguards which
wrap around each Ian individually, and exempts mesh liners.

Section 1, subdivision establishes the ban on sales, leases, or offers
for sale or lease of all crib bumper pads.

Section 1, subdivision 3, paragraph (a) provides that on or after the
effective date of this section, no child care facility or place of
public accommodation may use or have on its premises any crib bumper
pads unless a medical professional has determined that the use of bumper
pads is medically necessary for a particular child. Paragraph (b) of
this subdivision states that the office of children and family services
will notify child care facilities of the provisions in this subdivision.
Paragraph (c) provides that the office of children and family services
shall establish rules to comply with the ban on crib bumper pads in
child care facilities.

Section 1, subdivision 4 establishes the provisions for a violation of
subdivision 2 of this section. A court may impose a civil penalty of not
more than $500 for each violation.

Section 1, subdivision S states that provisions of this section are
severable and that if any provision of this section is held to be uncon-
stitutional, such invalidity will not affect other provisions that can
be given effect without the invalid provision.

Section 2 provides the effective date.

 
JUSTIFICATION:

The American Academy of Pediatrics and the American Sudden Infant Death
Syndrome Institute have both issued warnings regarding the dangers of
crib bumper pads and have urged parents not to use them.  Bumper pads
pose a. risk of death or serious injury because babies can get caught in
the fabric and suffocate.

A study recently published in the Journal of Pediatrics reports that
nationwide, twenty-three babies died between 2006 and 2012 from suffoca-
tion associated with the use of crib bumper pads. This number is three
times higher than the number of deaths attributable to crib bumper pads
which were recorded in the three previous six-year time spans. Forty-
eight babies died as a result of having bumper pads in their cribs from
1985 through 2012. During this twenty-seven year time period, an addi-
tional 146 infants were reported to have sustained serious injuries from
crib bumper pads, including choking on the bumper pad ties or nearly
suffocating.

Banning the sale of crib bumper pads would silence any confusion as to
their safety. Stores often display cribs decorated with bumper pads
which can lead to the assumption that they are in fact safe.  Prohibit-
ing the sale of crib bumper pads and their use in certain settings would
help to avoid preventable infant deaths and ensure children's safety in
their cribs.

 
PRIOR LEGISLATIVE HISTORY:

2017-18: S4055-B/A4151-A - RULES/passed assembly
A.9186-B,2016 passed Assembly.
Same as S.7041-A, 2016 referred to rules.

 
FISCAL IMPLICATIONS:

No fiscal impact to the State.

 
EFFECTIVE DATE:
This act shall take effect on the sixtieth day after it shall have
become a law.
